issues.claim: The gradient gives a direction, never a distance.
issues.problem: 3Blue1Brown says the gradient's component magnitudes show which changes matter more and its length reflects steepness; only the actual step size is set separately by the learning rate.
issues.fix: The gradient gives a direction and a steepness, but not how big a step to take.

issues.claim: On average it points the right way, because the errors cancel out.
issues.problem: Source says a mini-batch gradient is only a pretty good approximation of the true gradient, not exact; 'cancel out' is loose.
issues.fix: It is a noisy estimate, but a pretty good one, and on average it points the right way.

issues.claim: Weights attached to quiet neurons barely change.
issues.problem: Source says weights tied to small activations have a weaker effect on the cost, so they get smaller nudges; 'barely' is stronger than stated.
issues.fix: Weights attached to quiet neurons get smaller nudges.

issues.claim: The network never memorized an answer.
issues.problem: Networks can memorize training data (overfitting); the true point is that no answer is stored by hand.
issues.fix: Nobody handed the network an answer, it just got a little less wrong each time.

issues.claim: nudged slightly less wrong, millions of times
issues.problem: Sources do not give a step count; the number of updates depends on the training run.
issues.fix: My claim: the network never learns an answer, it gets nudged slightly less wrong, again and again.
